key_insight: Spatial-TTT uses test-time training on incoming video to continually adapt a compact spatial memory, selecting and retaining salient scene evidence so systems can maintain accurate spatial intelligence from an unbounded visual stream.
problem_solved: How to streamingly select, organize, and retain spatial information from long or unbounded video streams—going beyond larger context windows to keep a concise, up-to-date spatial representation.
method: Streaming spatial memory: maintain a compact, updateable spatial representation (e.g., metric/top-down map or memory slots) that is incrementally updated with each frame.

Test-time training (TTT): adapt model weights online using self-supervised objectives on incoming frames (e.g., view-consistency, reconstruction, contrastive signals) so representations align with the current environment.
Selective retention & organization: prioritize salient evidence via selection/pruning and balance plasticity vs stability so important spatial cues persist while noisy/obsolete data is discarded.
impact: Enables continual, real-world spatial reasoning for robotics, AR, and embodied agents by providing an efficient way to adapt and maintain spatial maps from live video without storing huge context windows—improving robustness to environment shifts and long-term deployment.

paper_title: Spatial-TTT: Streaming Visual-based Spatial Intelligence with Test-Time Training
paper_authors: Fangfu Liu, Diankun Wu, Jiawei Chi, Yimo Cai, Yi-Hsin Hung
